stories.headline: The World Cup Comes to Lumen Field — Next Match Monday
stories.body: Seattle is hosting six FIFA World Cup 2026 matches at Lumen Field, and the action is far from over. Belgium vs. Egypt kicks off Monday, June 15 at noon PT, followed by the USA vs. Australia on Juneteenth (June 19), Qatar vs. Bosnia-Herzegovina on June 24, and more through July. Fan celebration hubs at Pioneer Square, Seattle Center, and Victory Hall near Lumen Field offer giant screens, beer gardens, and live entertainment for ticketless fans too.

stories.headline: Belle and Sebastian Bring 30th Anniversary Magic to ZooTunes
stories.body: Tonight's the night — Belle and Sebastian's 30th Anniversary Tour of 'If You're Feeling Sinister' lands at Woodland Park Zoo's ZooTunes stage on Sunday, June 14 at 6 PM, with openers Quasi along for the ride. There is arguably no more Seattle way to spend a June evening than watching Scottish indie-pop legends play under the pines while peacocks wander nearby.
stories.location: Phinney Ridge · Sunday, June 14 at 6 PM

stories.headline: The Play That Goes Wrong Is Gloriously Going Wrong at Seattle Rep
stories.body: Seattle Rep's production of 'The Play That Goes Wrong' — a slapstick musical comedy in which actors stage a disaster-prone murder mystery — opened June 13 and runs through the month with special events including Pride night, ASL-interpreted performances, and a community celebration of Mexican culture. If you like your theater with pratfalls and flying set pieces, this is your show.

stories.headline: Hike Seattle's Best Trails for Just $3 via Trailhead Direct
stories.body: King County Metro's Trailhead Direct bus service is back through August 30, connecting Seattleites to some of the region's finest hiking trails on Saturdays, Sundays, and select holidays for just $3 each way — kids 18 and under ride free. It's the easiest excuse to swap your Sunday screen time for old-growth forest and mountain views, no car required.

stories.headline: Juneteenth Freedom Festival at Jimi Hendrix Park Is Free for All
stories.body: On Friday, June 19, Jimi Hendrix Park in the Central District hosts the Juneteenth Freedom Festival from noon to 8 PM — a free, all-ages celebration featuring Grammy-nominated soul artist Marsha Ambrosius of Floetry, live performances, food and local vendors, and family programming. The day holds extra electricity this year: it also marks the 10th anniversary of Africatown Community Land Trust and coincides with the USA vs. Australia World Cup match.
stories.location: Central District · Friday, June 19, noon–8 PM

stories.headline: Free Summer Concerts Return to the Ballard Locks Lawn
stories.body: Through September 27, the historic Hiram M. Chittenden Locks in Ballard hosts free weekend concerts on the lawn every Saturday, Sunday, and Labor Day. Pack a picnic and a blanket, stake out a patch of grass beside the locks, and let the boats — and the music — drift by. The series runs rain-permitting, so check the forecast before you head out.
